$comment: Fields Polaris serves to Nova, per response object.
Nova and Polaris ship from separate repositories on separate schedules, and both
sides address these fields by string literal. Nothing in either build can see the
other, so a rename on one side degrades silently: a reader falls back to its
default and the feature quietly stops working rather than failing.
This manifest is the shared record. tests/integration/test_nova_contract.cpp keeps
Polaris honest about it, and scripts/check-nova-contract.py diffs it against a Nova
checkout. Adding a field to a response means adding it here in the same commit.
Drift found when this manifest was introduced, on 2026-08-06, is recorded under
known_drift so it is tracked rather than rediscovered.
Schema format 2 is additive: ordered fields and legacy nova_reader entries remain. Only generated:true objects use generated names in S1a; wire object versions are unchanged.

js_outputs declares generated browser modules by name; an object defaults to default and may select js_output. Output paths stay under web/generated. Restricted outputs list their only allowed direct importers; other feature code uses those audited readers. Splitting outputs keeps lazy feature keys out of the initial shared module.
The informational clients[].video_queue object in stream_stats, served only for a registered host-session generation.

evicted_frames counts encoded frames removed at queue capacity for the evicted packet's live owner, even when another session produced the replacement. It is cumulative for that generation, not client network loss; normal pop, stop and destruction do not count.

The host video queue is shared across sessions. Browser video queues use the same oldest-only policy but have no host-session destination and are not included in these per-client counters. Stopped, expired and unregistered owners cannot write a live row.
One entry of live_tuning_history, bounded to 64 entries with version 1. Diagnostic kind/cause are open strings, distinct from Live Tuning status states.
fec_transition is optional allocation/encoder evidence, not delivered parity or physical FEC benefit. No Nova production reader at exact 3f6b6908 consumes history.
Optional history-entry fec_transition. Integers describe nominal configured/published actuator allocation; phases are fixed, lowering_rate or raising_rate.
Pending percentages are integer or explicit null (no pending transaction). A positive from_frame_index is present only for actual published raises at their accepted next-frame boundary.
For example, restoring parity from 15 to 10 precedes the higher encoder ACK; restored confirmation from 10 to 10 has no new publication boundary. Absence means unavailable, never zero.
GET /polaris/v1/spaces, and the body of POST /polaris/v1/spaces/select. What one
paired device may see, and why what it cannot do is off. schema stays 1: every key
added after nova#308 is optional, and the six state words on each space never grow,
because PolarisSpaces.parse nulls the whole payload on a value it does not know.

spaces_capacity.$comment: The capacity object of spaces_snapshot and of the console's /api/multiseat/profiles: the trusted seat budget summed over every GPU, so a client can say "one Space at a time" before a launch is refused.

space.$comment: One entry of spaces_snapshot.spaces. state is one of ready, starting, running, stopping, in_use, unavailable and must stay so; can_open and blocked_reason carry what state cannot (a full budget).

space_library.$comment: GET /polaris/v1/spaces/library?space_id=. The games are space_library_game objects.

$comment: One Space library game, parsed by the ordinary game readers. Shared served fields borrow game names; absent game fields remain explicit existing reader defaults in known_drift.

space_ref.$comment: The space object of space_library_game. Nova requires it on every space.* id and checks id and target against the id it parsed.

space_launch_mode.$comment: The launch_mode of a Space game, fixed to gamescope_stream; a four-field subset of launch_mode read by the same modeJson reader. Space entries deliberately omit follows_host_default, launch_as, launch_as_available and launch_as_unavailable_reason, and that shared reader defaults each one when absent: follows_host_default to true, launch_as to no app launch-as contract (it checks whether any of the three launch_as keys exists first), launch_as_available to null and launch_as_unavailable_reason to an empty string. The four intentional omissions and their exact reader defaults are declared in known_drift with a per-object reason. Format 2 records these same intentional omissions and exact reader defaults under subset_of/omitted; known_drift.$detail preserves the prior source-reconciliation reason.

follows_host_default.reason: Space mode is fixed to gamescope_stream and the legacy readers take an absent follows_host_default as true. This preserves current UI behavior; changing its meaning is a separate owner decision.

launch_as.reason: None of the three per-app Launch As keys is served, so all readers use the older-host path rather than inventing a per-app Launch As contract.

launch_as_available.reason: No per-app Launch As availability is declared for this Space entry.

launch_as_unavailable_reason.reason: With no per-app Launch As contract, the old reader default is the empty string.

space_legacy_game.$comment: The one entry GET /polaris/v1/games serves to a device routed to a Space on a host without the Space library: the fixed profile app identity that NovaSpaceUiState.singleSpace opens.

host-authoritative launch-mode catalog (per-mode availability, server
labels, disable reasons, and the private/host grouping). Guarded because
the client-settings surface carried the picker feed with zero drift

group/unavailable_reason and the runtime/capture/topology vocabulary
ship ahead of their Nova consumer - see known_drift.
The non-Linux catalog has no session_overridable, so it is optional.
One entry of capabilities.encoders in GET /polaris/v1/client-settings and
encoder_backends in GET /polaris/v1/capabilities. Availability describes
what the running build can select; every request is validated again against
the live capture route at launch. Auto alone may fall back.
Top-level GET /optimize deterministic launch resolver response.
append_deterministic_optimization_json emits the selected preset, the
authoritative nested field provenance, and temporary flat compatibility
values. History, recovery records, and AI output cannot define these
settings. ai_explanation is typed informational output only.
The exact session encoder selection nested under encoder_resolution in a
deterministic /optimize response. Nova binds requested, resolved, lock, and
fallback policy to the final launch. The concrete active backend remains
informational because Auto is resolved only by the live launch probe.
Exact app and topology identity bound to a deterministic optimize result.
Nova rejects a preflight or fresh result unless the canonical app id,
host-default or explicit topology request, lock state, and Steam desktop
choice all match the launch that will consume it. Source, reason, and
normalization metadata make paired, app, and host capability decisions
auditable without allowing them to become client-authored policy.
One entry in resolved_profile.fields. Nova rejects the value unless
all provenance metadata is present with the expected primitive types.
A trusted launch envelope requires display_mode plus display_width,
display_height, target_fps, target_bitrate_kbps, and hdr. Component
display provenance is authoritative when a preset composes paired
dimensions with an explicit cadence lock. Source is allowlisted and
history or AI provenance is never accepted as launch authority.

host_power.$comment: Served on the capabilities response and on GET /polaris/v1/host/power. Tells a client whether to offer a sleep control at all: sleep_supported is what logind answers, sleep_enabled is the host owner's opt in, and sleep_permitted is whether this client may control the host rather than only watch it. All three have to be true before the control is worth showing. The last_sleep_* fields carry what became of the previous request, which is a different fact from whether it was accepted: logind returns as soon as a suspend is queued, and a task that will not freeze can abort the suspend afterwards.

$comment: The pyrowave_bitrate object of GET /polaris/v1/session/status, present only while the stream
codec is PyroWave. The advice fields are PyroWave's model for the stream's shape, as
requests: what a client sets so the encoder lands on the model's rate after FEC, audio and
overhead. advice_far_kbps is H 2.875, a device's own screen, at far_target_db, 31 dB,
calibrated on a Retroid Pocket 6, and the lower figure; advice_near_kbps is H 2.0, a
television or monitor, at target_db, the author's 35 dB. Both are the model's readouts and
neither is capped. What the host recommends is raise_goal_kbps, what Doctor raises to: the
far figure capped at cap_kbps and max_bitrate. encoder_kbps is the rate the encoder runs at
now, and request_kbps the same rate as a request, what a client sets to land the encoder
there. ceiling_frame_share is the share of recent frames at 99% of the byte budget (null
while unknown). It never makes a stream starved, and decides only Doctor's finding for a
stream the cap or max_bitrate holds below advice_far_kbps. starved is the host's verdict:
request_kbps is below 90% of raise_goal_kbps. assumes names the FEC share and audio cost the
requests were grossed up for: the stream's own, as its bitrate_units carry them, and the
host's FEC share with stereo in high quality until its handshake is recorded. Its advice
names are pyrowave_advice's (names_from); Android and Deck read both with one parser each.
The response of GET /polaris/v1/pyrowave/advice?width=&height=&fps=&chroma=420|444, announced
by features.pyrowave_advice_v1. The same advice fields as pyrowave_bitrate, without the live
ones, for a shape a client is about to ask for: the model's readouts uncapped, and
raise_goal_kbps, the one the host recommends. available is false with a reason and a
message when the host cannot serve PyroWave: not_built carries no figures, no_vulkan_device
still carries them. assumes names the FEC share and audio cost the requests were grossed up
for: the asking client's own stream's, as its bitrate_units carry them, when it streams
here, and the host's FEC share with stereo in high quality when it does not. The 400
invalid_query body is an error, not this object.
The bitrate_units object of GET /polaris/v1/session/status, announced by
features.bitrate_units_v1 and present for every stream whatever its codec, once the stream's
handshake is recorded. A client's request covers the video, its FEC, the audio and packet
overhead, and the handshake hands the encoder what is left by the arithmetic formula names,
stream_bitrate_v1 (src/stream_bitrate.h): encoder_kbps_for_wire(split_kbps, fec_percentage,
audio_kbps) is encoder_kbps whenever split_kbps is not null, and wire_kbps_for_encoder
inverts it. requested_kbps is the client's own request, 0 when it sent none. split_kbps is
requested_kbps times warp_factor, cut to cap_kbps when a cap did (cap_kbps and cap_source
are null when none did), and null for a stream whose encoder rate is no split of its own
request: a watcher at its owner's rate, or a client that sent no bitrate. encoder_kbps is
where the handshake left the encoder, live_encoder_kbps the rate the encoder runs at now
after a live bitrate, Live Tuning or Doctor, fec_percentage the host's share when the
stream started. A client with a stream here gets that stream or nothing; one with no stream
here gets the first stream that recorded its handshake. A Space's stream carries none yet.
features.manual_bitrate_max_kbps, a number rather than a flag, is the most a client may set
by hand through client settings, a live bitrate, a resolved launch, a Space's resolver or the
launch profile route: 500000 from 1.5.0. A host without it takes 300000, so a client offers
more only to a host that announces it. No nova_reader yet.
Served at doctor.ai_explanation_request on GET /polaris/v1/session/status (#613). A pure
descriptor of whether the current Doctor reading can be explained on one explicit paired POST
/polaris/v1/doctor/explanation; it allocates, captures and starts nothing. enabled is host
opt-in with a fully configured provider, permitted is _allow_view plus sole active ownership of
exactly this app session, and available is everything else the POST checks again on its own.
finding_fingerprint and controller_revision are comparison metadata for that POST, never
authority, and stay empty and 0 without a permitted scope. features.doctor_ai_explanation_v1
says only that the protocol exists.
Every response of POST /polaris/v1/doctor/explanation (#613), success and fallback alike: at
most 8 KiB and Cache-Control no-store. status is true only with code explained and a non-null
explanation; otherwise fallback is true, explanation null and expires_in_ms 0, and the client
keeps its deterministic Doctor. changed is always false and authority explanation_only, because
nothing on the host moves. The request tuple is echoed only for an authorized, well-formed
request, and snapshot_id is allocated only once a POST was admitted.
The explanation of a successful doctor_ai_explanation_response (#613): the host-configured
provider's six fields after strict validation, per-field code point and UTF-8 caps, plain-text
checks and redaction. Informational prose only, never a setting, target value, action or the
Doctor's confidence grade.

Optional native_reception on paired own-current controller session status only, after matching RTSP version/session-ID/encrypted control13+v2. Both existing video encryption modes supported without changing encryption policy. Absence means unavailable/unnegotiated, never clean media.

Version1 observes queue-accepted original native packets separately from frame_submission and Java/media counters. All reasons/loop/packet kinds are fixed enumerations; no controller consumes this object.

host_report_age_ms is host-local. Reports and every sampled sender boundary expire after2s; no rejected report refreshes state. Zero, incomplete, gaps, sparse samples and clock failure remain explicit. Raw host timestamps and identities are not serialized.

media_authenticated comes only from actual host session video flags; control_authenticated becomes true only after verified encrypted control dispatch. Unencrypted video has on-path integrity limitations; accepted-original facts never authorize capacity/clean/recovery or a writer.

retention_limited is a fresh unavailable observation when lost unsampled sender retention prevents proving an aggregate bound; derived fields are cleared. Complete-class or matched-sample contradictions still reject without state/freshness mutation. Per-class evicted-frame high-water metadata is fixed-size and generation-local.

Untrusted connection-local native acceptance facts. Counters cover observer commits; they are not a packet-loss denominator, kernel ingress or capacity. interval_us and age units are microseconds; UINT32_MAX age means unavailable/saturated.

flags1 HAS_ACCEPTED,2 INCOMPLETE,4 CLOCK_UNAVAILABLE,8 TIMING_SAMPLE_LIMIT. Complete intervals <=2s. Longer incomplete reports have no samples or derived metrics; zero-time clock sentinel disables observation until a new native connection.

At most16 native originals, never FEC reconstructions. Sample age is report-end minus userspace socket-read timestamp, can predate acceptance interval, bounded2s. Exact frame32+RTP16 matches use a fixed16384x32-byte host ledger.

Derived packet_kind(data/parity),UDP payload bytes and host API duration require every packet and the entire accepted frame range to join one exact immutable tuple. Missing/stale/ambiguous/fallback/mixed data carries no derived values.

Optional dispersion bounds use only time differences: receive_delta-(endB-beginA) through receive_delta-(beginB-endA). They include batch/kernel/receiver scheduling and clock skew, not absolute one-way delay, media RTT or pure network queue. Reordered pairs carry no dispersion.

Exact immutable sender encoder tuple, diagnostic only. Every retained frame in inclusive first..last must be successful/fresh and tuple-equal; same kbps with different application sequence or origin is mixed. No control value or permission follows.
Owner-console passive Epic setup v1; no launch/adoption authority or identifying native details.

Source-wide launcher_closed is not selected-title ready. Prerequisites remain typed unknown until a complete trusted passive support binding exists; omission never implies support. Sampled preflight is checked again at launch. Receipt is historical same-launcher scan bookends, not continuous presence.

bounds.epoch: opaque process epoch, at most 64 ASCII characters; empty when no idle sample is available
bounds.sample_age_ms: nonnegative elapsed time from request start; no session or launcher duration

Owner-console passive Epic setup v1; no launch/adoption authority or identifying native details.

Owner-console passive Epic setup v1; no launch/adoption authority or identifying native details.
The optional vrr object of GET /polaris/v1/session/status: the variable-refresh record of the
asking client's own stream, stream_stats::vrr_json for the generation that response names as
session_generation. It is served whether Doctor v2 is enabled, still collecting or off, and is
absent when that stream has no record or the client has no live stream here: another client's,
a Watch row's or an ended session's record never stands in for it, and nothing is defaulted.
A Watch stream's own record says so itself (fallback_reason watch_or_input_only). schema is 1.
requested is the admitted request (true, false, malformed or absent) and requested_from launch
or resume, both frozen for the generation. host_permission is the host's frozen permission to
source-pace this stream, not proof that it does. effective is true only for a host source-time
sample at most 2 seconds old on a stream that has not ended; fallback_reason is null exactly
then. pacing_mode is fixed_grid, source_time_pending, unverified or source_time; capture_pacing
is unknown unless the host's own receipt proves source_driven. host_pacing appears once the
host has permission and has recorded a pacing receipt for the stream; host_adaptive_sync is
null without accepted capture timing. None of this is receiver presentation or physical
acceptance. clients[].vrr and last_session.vrr of the stream statistics share this shape and
emitter but carry stream_instance_id instead of session_generation. Readers are declared ahead
of their Nova implementations (papi-ux/nova#241 Linux, #242 Android); the paired
check-nova-contract.py reports them unavailable until those readers land.
The host_pacing object inside session_vrr: the host's latest source-pacing receipt for that
stream. state is waiting, source_time, latched_fallback or unsupported. fresh is true only for
a sample at most 2 seconds old on a stream that has not ended. last_event and event_counts
(keyed by event name) are diagnostic. receiver_presentation_verified, physical_acceptance and
receiver_source_cadence_available are always false: the host proves none of them.
trace_receipts, a diagnostic watermark object, appears only while the trace watermark is
accepted. Readers are declared ahead of their Nova implementations, as for session_vrr.
Corrected 2026-08-07. The first version of this file was written against the
working tree of a Nova checkout that was 295 commits divergent from origin/master,
and scoped reads by receiver name rather than by function. Both errors inflated it.
Verified against origin/master with function scoping, Nova reads every field Polaris

Space id, name and state are read explicitly with getString; can_open uses has/opt/getBoolean, and the top-level capacity is read with json.opt. The eight-entry stale-declaration cleanup removes these five from known unread fields.

default_space_id, unavailable_reason, switch_blocked_reason and blocked_reason are read through optionalWord, which this scan does not resolve. Their remaining known entries describe a scanner limitation, not absent runtime consumers.

library_available, space_name and total on space_library are informational; Nova checks status and space_id and reads the games. worker_profile on the legacy entry is never read: NovaSpaceUiState.singleSpace keys on the fixed id.

game.space is read by the shared adapter and served only on space_library_game, where it is declared; the ordinary library never carries it. serverinfo PolarisSpacesAvailable is XML written through the property tree, outside this manifest extraction.

linux_gpu_profile object instead, so the same fields on capture are redundant rather
than missed. An earlier revision recorded them as drift because linux_gpu_profile was
linux_gpu_profile: Resolved. Nova read vaapi_vendor and Polaris never served it; vaapi.cpp logged the
string at encoder creation without publishing it. It is now recorded in stats and
served in this object, which is what names the driver generation in a crash report.
game: platform and runtime are served from the Lutris runner persisted at import, and for

psp, gba as platform; the preset id as runtime), with platform_label and

requires the typed resolved-profile envelope before they can affect launch.
space_launch_mode: Space games deliberately serve only preferred_mode, allowed_modes, recommended_mode and mode_reason. Nova uses the shared modeJson adapter and tolerates the four omitted fields: follows_host_default defaults to true, launch_as is null when none of the three launch_as keys exists, launch_as_available defaults to null, and launch_as_unavailable_reason defaults to an empty string. These are declared compatibility defaults, not evidence of hardware or UI acceptance.
